question: Should OpenClaw adopt the fail-closed injected-reader boundary and the proposed focused media-base64/MIME/audio additions as permanent public Plugin SDK contracts?
rationale: The implementation is coherent and policy-aligned, but it intentionally changes an existing reader capability and expands the shipped external plugin API; repository policy reserves those compatibility and ownership choices for an explicit owner decision.

options.title: Approve the narrow contracts
options.body: Approve the explicit-root requirement and focused additive SDK surfaces, then review the clean conflict resolution and refreshed validation before merge.

options.title: Keep helpers internal
options.body: Retain the WhatsApp hardening but remove or reduce the new public SDK surface until another external plugin demonstrates the contract is needed.

options.title: Preserve reader compatibility
options.body: Keep the prior injected-reader behavior temporarily with a named migration or deprecation plan instead of changing it unconditionally.

recommendation.title: Approve the narrow contracts
recommendation.body: Approve the explicit-root requirement and focused additive SDK surfaces, then review the clean conflict resolution and refreshed validation before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged history shows the strongest involvement in both WhatsApp outbound security behavior and shared plugin/media boundaries.
